statement_utf8:
Let $\nu$ denote the paper's robustness measure for systems with structured uncertainties, and let arbitrary precision mean that the computed value can be made to have any prescribed accuracy.

**Polynomial-time computation conjecture.** There exists a polynomial-time algorithm to compute $\nu$ within arbitrary precision.

Such an algorithm would make the proposed robustness measure computationally tractable for large-scale systems and complement the distributed methods developed for its convex upper bound. The source states this as a concluding research conjecture and supplies no algorithm or proof establishing it.
technical_screen: Existential polynomial-time arbitrary-accuracy claim needs the exact uncertainty structure, encoding and dependence on log(1/epsilon). No finite numerical nu instance decides this uniform complexity claim; primary body not inspected.

statement_utf8:
Let $f(n,m)$ be the largest integer such that every graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges has a chordal subgraph with at least $f(n,m)$ edges. For $k\geq 2$, let $t_k(n)$ denote the number of edges in the balanced complete $k$-partite graph on $n$ vertices. Let $n\geq 1$ and suppose that

$$
t_k(n)+1\leq m\leq t_{k+1}(n).
$$

**The maximal chordal subgraph conjecture.** Then

$$
f(n,m)=\min_{t,r}\bigl(kn-t+r\bigr)-\binom{k+1}{2},
$$

where the minimum is taken over all $t,r\geq 0$ satisfying

$$
t_{k-1}(n-t)+t(n-t)+t_2(r)\geq m.
$$

The paper determines $f(n,m)$ asymptotically for all $m$ and exactly when $m\leq t_3(n)+1$; this conjecture proposes the exact value throughout the remaining ranges of $m$.
technical_screen: Exact minimax over every n,m in every Turan interval k>=2. A single graph could refute a lower bound but proving f requires all graphs and an extremal construction. No concrete small obstruction identified; t,r domains also need primary confirmation.

statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $Delta(G)$, and let $s$ be a positive integer. In the one-cop, $s$-robber damage game, the cop saves $k$ vertices if the optimal damage satisfies $\operatorname{dmg}(G;s)\leq |V(G)|-k$.

**Multi-robber damage conjecture.** For all $s>2$, if

$$
\Delta(G)\geq \binom{s}{2}+2,
$$

then the cop can save three vertices against $s$ robbers.

For two robbers, the corresponding result is known under the weaker condition $\Delta(G)\geq 3$. The conjecture proposes a sufficient maximum-degree condition for saving three vertices with more than two robbers; its status is not established in the supplied text.
technical_screen: For every s>2 and every graph of maximum degree at least binomial(s,2)+2, one cop must save three. A bounded pursuit simulation would require exact move/damage conventions and does not give the all-s strategy. No uniform strategy found.

statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be a $3$-connected graph. A set $W\subset V(G)$ is **contractible** if $G(W)$ is connected and $G-W$ is $2$-connected; a contractible set with $k$ vertices is called a $k$-contractible set. **McCuaig–Ota conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists an integer $n$ such that every $3$-connected graph $G$ on at least $n$ vertices has a $k$-contractible set.

The conjecture asks whether sufficiently large $3$-connected graphs always contain contractible sets of every prescribed finite size. The paper proves the assertion for $k\geqslant 5$ under the minimum-degree condition $\delta(G)\geqslant \left[\frac{2k+1}{3}\right]+2$, while the unrestricted conjecture remains open in the supplied text.
technical_screen: For each k a size threshold must work for every 3-connected graph. Checking k or adding minimum degree proves only an instance or restricted family. No full-scope contraction mechanism found.

statement_utf8:
For $\delta>0$, let $\rho(3,6,\delta)$ be the limiting maximum edge density of an $n$-vertex graph with independence number at most $\delta n$ that admits a red/blue coloring with no red $K_3$ and no blue $K_6$. **Kim–Kim–Liu's conjecture.** For sufficiently small $\delta>0$,

$$
\rho(3,6,\delta)=\frac{5}{12}+\frac{\delta}{2}+2\delta^2.
$$

The source describes the right-hand side as attained by a construction, so the conjecture concerns the matching upper bound for sufficiently small $\delta$.
technical_screen: Requires a sharp Ramsey-Turan upper density for all sufficiently small positive delta. Source-supplied lower construction is not the missing upper bound; no short stability route identified.

statement_utf8:
For $\delta>0$, let $\rho(3,7,\delta)$ be the limiting maximum edge density of an $n$-vertex graph with independence number at most $\delta n$ that admits a red/blue coloring with no red $K_3$ and no blue $K_7$. **The $(K_3,K_7)$ density conjecture.** For sufficiently small $\delta>0$,

$$
\rho(3,7,\delta)=\frac{7}{16}+\frac{\delta}{2}.
$$

The source gives a construction proving the corresponding lower bound. The conjecture is the assertion that this construction is asymptotically optimal for sufficiently small $\delta$.
technical_screen: Requires the matching upper bound 7/16+delta/2 throughout a positive interval near zero. Finite colored graphs and the stated construction do not certify the limiting supremum.

statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $\chi_{\rm pcf}(G)$ be its conflict-free chromatic number, the least number of colours in a proper vertex colouring such that every vertex has a neighbour whose colour occurs exactly once in its neighbourhood.

**Caro–Petru1evski–skrekovski's conjecture.** For every connected graph $G$ of maximum degree $\Delta\geq 3$,

$$
\chi_{\rm pcf}(G)\leq \Delta+1.
$$

This conjecture strengthens the known general upper bound $\chi_{\rm pcf}(G)\leq\left\lfloor 5\Delta/2\right\rfloor$ and is the central conflict-free colouring problem addressed asymptotically in the paper. The text indicates that it is proved when the minimum degree is sufficiently large relative to $\log\Delta$, while the unrestricted case remains open.
technical_screen: All connected graphs with Delta>=3, not just large minimum degree. Leaves and mixed degrees prevent applying the stated asymptotic hypothesis directly; no Delta+1 proper conflict-free recoloring invariant found.

statement_utf8:
For every positive integer $n$, let

$$
\operatorname{inv}(n)=\max\{\operatorname{inv}(D)\mid D\text{ is an oriented graph of order }n\}.
$$

Here $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ is the minimum number of inversions needed to transform $D$ into an acyclic oriented graph.

**Belkhechine et al.'s inversion-number conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{inv}(n)\geq\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This strengthens the elementary counting lower bound given immediately before it and asserts that the logarithmic loss in that bound is unnecessary. The source does not state a resolution.
technical_screen: An oriented graph with inv>=floor((n-1)/2) must exist for every n. Finite inversion enumeration would only settle fixed orders; no construction with a uniform rank obstruction to all shorter inversion sequences identified.

statement_utf8:
Let $\tau(D)$ denote the minimum size of a vertex set whose deletion makes an oriented graph $D$ acyclic, and let $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ denote its inversion number.

**Bang-Jensen et al.'s tightness conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, there exists an oriented graph $D$ such that

$$
\tau(D)=n\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{inv}(D)=2n.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the general bound $\operatorname{inv}(D)\leq2\tau(D)$ is tight for every positive value of the cycle-transversal number; the paper notes it would follow from the dijoin conjecture. The source does not state a resolution.
technical_screen: For every positive n both exact tau=n and exact inv=2n must hold. Disjoint union alone has no established inversion additivity bridge here. No proof of simultaneous lower bounds found.

statement_utf8:
For an oriented graph $D$ and a vertex subset $V_i$, write $D\langle V_i\rangle$ for the subdigraph induced by $V_i$; let $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ denote inversion number.

**Alon's inversion-number partition conjecture.** For every two positive integers $k_1,k_2$, there exists an integer $f(k_1,k_2)$ such that every oriented graph $D$ with

$$
\operatorname{inv}(D)\geq f(k_1,k_2)
$$

 admits a partition $(V_1,V_2)$ of $V(D)$ satisfying

$$
\operatorname{inv}(D\langle V_i\rangle)\geq k_i\quad\text{for }i=1,2.
$$

This asks for an inversion-number analogue of Alon's minimum-out-degree partition conjecture: sufficiently large global inversion number should force both parts to retain prescribed inversion complexity. The source does not state a resolution.
technical_screen: Needs f(k1,k2) for every positive pair and every oriented graph above its threshold. A small partition check does not bound f; no hereditary obstruction or induction controlling both parts found.

statement_utf8: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite union-closed family of sets, and let $M$ be its largest set. Assume that for every pair of elements $a,b\in M$, the family contains a set $A$ with $|A\cap\{a,b\}|=1$. Let $x$ be the only element belonging to at least half of the sets of $\mathcal{F}$. **Poonen's structural conjecture.** If $|M|\geq 2$, then $\mathcal{F}$ consists of $\emptyset$ together with precisely all subsets of $M$ containing $x$; if $|M|=1$, then $\mathcal{F}=\{\{x\}\}$ or $\mathcal{F}=\{\emptyset,\{x\}\}$. This is the equivalent formulation associated with the twin-free condition and is stated as open.
technical_screen: Finite separating union-closed family with exactly one half-frequent element must have the specified complete x-star plus empty set. The literal pair condition must mean distinct a,b; exploiting a=b would be wording only. No uniform structural derivation found.

statement_utf8: Let $G$ be a hierarchically hyperbolic group (HHG), and let $\partial_M G$ be its Morse boundary. Assume that $G$ admits a largest acylindrical action. The topology on $\partial_M G$ induced by this action is the topology of coarse convergence of hierarchy paths. **Coarse-convergence conjecture.** The topology on the Morse boundary of an HHG induced by its largest acylindrical action is the topology of coarse convergence of hierarchy paths. Largest acylindrical actions are known to exist for all hierarchically hyperbolic groups and to be $\kappa$-injective, but identifying the induced topology with coarse convergence of hierarchy paths remains open.
technical_screen: Equality of induced and coarse-convergence Morse-boundary topologies for every HHG. Literal statement repeats the conjecture as an assertion; source definitions of topology and largest action are needed. No topology comparison proved.

statement_utf8:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, let $G\Box H$ be their Cartesian product, and let $D$ be a dominating set of $G\Box H$. For each $h\in V(H)$, let $G_h$ be the $G$-layer corresponding to $h$, and let $p_G$ denote projection onto $G$. **The weaker Vizing conjecture.** If, for every $h\in V(H)$, there is a minimum dominating set $D_h$ of $G$ such that

$$
p_G(D\cap G_h)\subseteq D_h,
$$

then

$$
|D|\geq \gamma(G)\gamma(H).
$$

This is a special case of Vizing's conjecture, motivated by the paper's discussion of vertically undominated cells and equality in the general half-bound; the paper establishes related special cases but leaves this formulation as the object of conjectural interest.
technical_screen: All products and dominating sets satisfying a layerwise inclusion into possibly different minimum dominating sets. Those minimum sets need not share labels, so a common-coordinate pigeonhole argument lacks a bridge; no full layer-labeling proof found.

statement_utf8:
Let $\mathcal G^K$ denote the class of Gaussian-dependent vectors of $K$ p-values, and let $S_K(\mathbf P)$ be the Simes p-value for $\mathbf P$. Define

$$
s_K(\alpha):=\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal G^K}\mathbb P\bigl(S_K(\mathbf P)\leqslant\alpha\bigr).
$$

**Gaussian Simes bound.** There exists $c\geqslant 1$ such that

$$
s_K(\alpha)\leqslant c\alpha
$$

for all $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $K\in\mathbb N$.
If true, determining the smallest possible $c$, especially for practically relevant small values of $\alpha$, is important. The paper notes that the currently available general bound grows with $K$, so whether a universal constant exists remains open.
technical_screen: Uniform c independent of K and alpha across all Gaussian dependence matrices. Pairwise examples and general harmonic bounds do not give a universal constant. One/two-sided p-value construction needs primary definitions.

statement_utf8:
Let $\mathcal G^K$ be the class of Gaussian-dependent vectors of $K$ p-values, and let $S_K(\mathbf P)$ be the Simes p-value. Define

$$
s_K(\alpha):=\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal G^K}\mathbb P\bigl(S_K(\mathbf P)\leqslant\alpha\bigr).
$$

For the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure at level $\alpha$, let $f_K(\alpha)$ be the maximum false discovery rate over the possible numbers of true null hypotheses and Gaussian-dependent p-value vectors.
**Gaussian FDR–Simes equality.**

$$
f_K(\alpha)=s_K(\alpha)
$$

for all $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $K\in\mathbb N$.
The equality would identify the worst-case Gaussian FDR with the worst-case Gaussian Simes-test error probability. The paper explicitly says that it remains unclear whether these quantities are equal, so the claim is open.
technical_screen: Requires equality of two suprema for every K,alpha including configurations with false nulls. All-null Simes supplies only one direction; no extension preserving Gaussian structure for the opposite comparison identified.

statement_utf8:
Let $c'$ range over integers with $c'\not\equiv 3\pmod 7$, and consider the prime factorization of $3^{3+6c'}+1$. 

**Infinitude conjecture.** There are infinitely many values of $c'\not\equiv 3\pmod 7$ such that every prime other than $2$ and $7$ occurring in the factorization of $3^{3+6c'}+1$ has exponent congruent to $1\pmod 3$.

Such values of $c'$ would produce the polynomial families used to construct further twists of the Klein quartic that are counterexamples to the Hasse principle. The source provides no resolution of this arithmetic conjecture.
technical_screen: Infinitely many c-prime in the allowed residue classes with every non-2,7 valuation 1 mod 3. Negative c-prime make a nonintegral expression, a domain issue rather than a substantive result. Positive-exponent infinitude lacks a valuation-control mechanism.

statement_utf8:
Let $DPL(n,d)$ denote a diameter $d$ perfect Lee code in $\mathbb{Z}^{n}$. For odd $d$, this agrees with a perfect Lee code of radius $(d-1)/2$; for even $d$, it is defined using a tiling by maximum-size anticodes of diameter $d-1$. **Horak–AlBdaiwi conjecture.** There is no $DPL(n,d)$ code for $n\ge3$ and $d>4$, with the exception of the pair

$$
(n,d)=(3,6).
$$
 This is presented as an extension of the Golomb–Welch conjecture. Etzion proposed the problem in 2011, and Horak and AlBdaiwi formally presented the conjecture in 2012; the source does not state whether it has been resolved.
technical_screen: Nonexistence for all n>=3,d>4 except (3,6) includes broad Golomb-Welch-type tilings. Small anticodes or a single excluded pair do not give full nonexistence; no short obstruction found.

statement_utf8:
Let $S$ be an even set of points in the plane, and let $\{a_ib_i:i=1,\dots,n\}$ be a max-sum matching of $S$, where $|S|=2n$. A point $o$ is required to satisfy, for every matched pair, the sum of its distances to the pair's endpoints. **Fingerhut's conjecture.** There exists a point $o$ in the plane such that

$$
\|a_i-o\|+\|b_i-o\|\leq \frac{2}{\sqrt 3}\|a_i-b_i\|\qquad\text{for all }i=1,\dots,n.
$$

The factor $2/\sqrt 3$ is optimal, and the conjecture was introduced by Andy Fingerhut in connection with minimum Steiner stars; it was previously known with weaker factors and is proved in this paper.
technical_screen: For every planar max-sum matching the common ellipse point is exactly source Theorem 4 in arXiv2212.14200v1. Read Conjecture 1 context, Lemma 3 and Theorem 4 at fingerhut.txt lines 285-350. Author theorem scope defeats eligibility; full proof/dependency audit not claimed.

statement_utf8:
Let $k$ and $d$ be positive integers, let $\mu>0$, and let $h_d^{k-1}(k,n)$ be the minimum $d$-degree threshold for a Hamilton tight cycle in an $n$-vertex $k$-graph. Let $\textbf{G}=\{G_i\}_{i\in[n]}$ be a $k$-graph system, and let $\delta_d(G_i)$ denote the minimum $d$-degree of $G_i$.

**Rainbow minimum-threshold conjecture.** There exists $n_0$ such that, for every $n\geq n_0$, if

$$
\delta_d(G_i)\geq h_d^{k-1}(k,n)+\mu\binom{n}{d}
$$

for every $i\in[n]$, then $\textbf{G}$ admits a rainbow Hamilton cycle.

This conjecture proposes that, up to an additive error, the rainbow threshold agrees with the ordinary tight Hamilton-cycle threshold. The source gives no resolution, so it remains open.
technical_screen: All fixed k,d,mu and sufficiently large n. Error term binomial(n,d) versus usual degree scale binomial(n-d,k-d) and allowed d ranges need primary confirmation. Exploiting vacuity or a mistranscription is no outcome; no rainbow absorption proof found.

statement_utf8:
For each integer $k\geq2$, consider the Cartesian product $C_{2k}\square P_2$ of the cycle $C_{2k}$ and the path $P_2$. The notation $\operatorname{ex}(n,H)$ denotes the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no copy of $H$. **Even-prism exponent improvement conjecture.** For every $k\geq2$, there exists $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(k)>0$ such that

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,C_{2k}\square P_2)=O\left(n^{\frac53-\varepsilon}\right).
$$

This would improve the currently stated general upper bound $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_{2k}\square P_2)=O(n^{5/3})$; the paper presents the improvement as an open conjecture.
technical_screen: For each k>=2 some positive exponent improvement is required at all large n. The k=2 instance or a logarithmic improvement does not suffice; no uniform forbidden-prism counting argument identified.

statement_utf8:
For finite graphs $G$ and $H$, say that $G$ is **$H$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. Write $\omega(G)$ for the clique number and $\eta(G)$ for the minimum size of a set meeting every maximum stable set. A graph class is **$\eta$-bounded** if its members satisfy an upper bound on $\eta$ depending only on clique number.

**Gyárfás–Sumner analogue for $\eta$-boundedness.** For every forest $H$, there exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that every $H$-free graph $G$ satisfies $\eta(G)\leq f(\omega(G))$.

The conjecture is motivated by the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture and is known for stars and induced subgraphs of $P_4$, but remains open in general.
technical_screen: For every forest H a clique-number-only bound on a transversal of all maximum stable sets. Star/P4 reductions cover only source-known cases. No general forest induction preserving maximum stable sets found.

statement_utf8:
Let $E_k$ denote the limit of the expected width of the largest block-palindrome factorization of a length-$n$ word over an alphabet of size $k$, whose existence is established for every $k\geq 2$. Let $(a_i)_{i\geq 1}$ be the coefficient sequence in the formal expansion in powers of $k^{-1}$. **Coefficient conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 2$, 

$$
E_k=1+\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}a_i k^{-i},
$$

where the sequence $(a_n/2)_{n\geq 1}$ is OEIS sequence A274199. This conjecture identifies the empirically observed coefficients of the expected limiting width; the paper provides numerical evidence but does not establish the claimed coefficient sequence.
technical_screen: Exact all-k series identification. Read primary v1 section 3 including Lemma 3 proof, Theorem 4 and Conjecture 5, and v2 corresponding section. Greedy shortest-border renewal suggests q=sum_j u_j k^(-2j), E=(1+q)/(1-q), but neither the limit bridge nor identification with A274199 was proved or computed. OEIS primary request returned 403, stopped. Search snippet is not a sequence-definition or successor-proof clearance. No proposal.

statement_utf8:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph, and let a **dijoin** be a set of arcs meeting every dicut. A set of arcs is a $k$-dijoin if it can be decomposed into $k$ dijoins. Let $\tau\geq 2$ be an integer, and suppose every dicut of $D$ has size at least $\tau$.

**Weaker dijoin decomposition conjecture.** The arc set $A$ can be decomposed into a $k$-dijoin and a $(\tau-k)$-dijoin, for every $k\in\{1,\ldots,\tau-1\}$.

This is presented as a weaker variant of Woodall's conjecture, which asserts that the minimum size of a dicut equals the maximum number of pairwise disjoint dijoins and remains open. The case $k=1$ and $k=\tau-1$ is known, while the intermediate cases remain open.
technical_screen: Literal definition k-dijoin already means k disjoint dijoins, so splitting into k and tau-k would supply tau disjoint dijoins, apparently Woodall itself rather than a weaker form. Need actual source wording before any investment; no credit for a definition correction.

statement_utf8:
Let $f^{(r)}(n;s,k)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph containing no collection of $k$ edges spanning at most $s$ vertices. For positive integers $r$, $k$, and $t$, set $s=k(r-t)+t$. **Shangguan–Tamo conjecture.** For any positive integers $r$, $k$, and $t$, the limit

$$
\pi(r,t,k):=\lim\limits_{n \to \infty} n^{-t} f^{(r)}(n;k(r-t)+t,k)
$$

exists. This generalises the Brown–Erdős–Sós conjecture, corresponding to $r=3$ and $t=2$; the limit is known in several cases, including all even $k$ when $r$ is sufficiently large relative to $k$ and $t$, and $k\in\{5,7\}$ for all $r>t\ge 2$, but the general case remains open.
technical_screen: Limit existence for arbitrary positive r,k,t, not isolated Brown-Erdos-Sos parameters. Degenerate ranges should be checked in primary source but yield only domain corrections. No near-superadditivity at n^t scale identified.

statement_utf8: Let a **very exotic sphere** mean a homotopy sphere that does not bound a parallelizable manifold. The preceding results show that very exotic spheres exist in at least $99$ congruence classes of dimensions modulo $192$. **Wang–Xu conjecture.** Very exotic spheres exist in all dimensions greater than $4$, except dimensions $5$, $6$, $11$, $12$, $27$, $43$, $56$, and $61$. This conjecture concerns the detection of elements in the cokernel of the stable $\mathrm{J}$-homomorphism and would determine precisely the dimensions in which very exotic spheres occur. The low-dimensional computations of Isaksen, Wang, and Xu, together with work of Ravenel and recent results, verify it up to dimension $102$; the assertion remains open in general.
technical_screen: Existence in every nonexceptional dimension above 4 entails an infinite stable-homotopy detection problem. Known computations through 102 are not a full route; certificate would require large imported machinery.

statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be a finite primitive permutation group on $\Omega$, with point stabiliser $H$, and define

$$
\rho_0(G):=\max\left\{\frac{|K|}{|H|\sqrt{|\Omega|}}:K\leqslant G\text{ is a fixer}\right\}.
$$

**Uniform boundedness conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $c$ such that $\rho_0(G)<c$ for all finite primitive permutation groups $G$.
This conjecture asserts that the largest fixer, normalized by the order of a point stabiliser and the square root of the permutation degree, is uniformly bounded across all finite primitive permutation groups. Its status is not established in the supplied text.
technical_screen: One absolute bound across all primitive groups and all fixer subgroups. Primary definition of fixer and primitive product-action reductions are absent here; small group searches cannot settle unbounded families. No unbounded normalized construction found.

statement_utf8:
Let $F \colon \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2^n$ be an almost perfect nonlinear (APN) function, meaning that for every $a,b \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $a \ne 0$, the equation $F(x+a)+F(x)=b$ has either zero or two solutions. The **algebraic degree** of $F$ is the maximum degree of a monomial appearing in its algebraic normal form.

**Budaghyan–Carlet–Helleseth conjecture.** No APN function $F \colon \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2^n$ has algebraic degree $n$ for all $n \geq 3$.

APN functions are important in cryptography because they provide optimal resistance to differential attacks, and their graphs are Sidon sets. The conjecture is stated in the source as a completely open question.
technical_screen: Confirmed primary Conjecture 2.1 and ANF/APN definitions, apn.txt 430-485. Top ANF coefficient is XOR of all outputs, but APN derivative pair sums only show distinct derivative values; their XOR need not vanish from distinctness alone. No all-n parity proof obtained. Source-internal later APN/Sidon results were located, not fully audited.

statement_utf8:
Let $b_1(n)$ be the largest irreducible character degree of the symmetric group $S_n$, and for each $m\geq 2$ let $b_m(n)$ be the $m$-th largest irreducible character degree of $S_n$. **Submaximal character degree ratio conjecture.** For any fixed integer $m\geq 2$,

$$
\frac{b_m(n)}{b_1(n)}\to 1\quad\text{as }n\to\infty.
$$

This conjecture asserts that symmetric groups have no single character degree that remains asymptotically separated from the other largest degrees; the paper presents experimental evidence for the analogous behavior of the second and third largest degrees, but does not provide a proof for arbitrary fixed $m$.
technical_screen: For every fixed m>=2 the ordered character-degree ratio must approach 1 as n tends to infinity. Conjugate partitions may duplicate degrees, and the intended distinctness ordering needs primary confirmation. Hook-length perturbations need uniform control near maximizing diagrams; none proved.

statement_utf8:
Let $d$ be a positive integer, let $N_1,N_2,\dots,N_d$ be the side lengths of a $d$-dimensional setting, and let $k$ be the number of eggs. Write $P_d(k)$ for the minimum number of drops required in the worst-case scenario under the strategy considered in the paper.

**Recursive upper-bound conjecture.** In a $d$-dimensional setting,

$$
P_d(k)\leq\left\lceil (k-d+1)\cdot(N_1+N_2+\dots+N_d)^{1/(k-d+1)}\right\rceil,
$$

for $k\geq d$.

The conjecture extrapolates the recursive upper bounds established in the one-, two-, and three-dimensional cases to arbitrary dimension. It concerns the performance of the same critical-point strategy in the worst case; the general $d$-dimensional claim is presented as suggested by the lower-dimensional pattern, with no resolution supplied here.
technical_screen: Read eggs v1 conjecture and adjacent 2D recursive proof. All d,k>=d and side lengths are required. Source induction has continuous optimized step sizes; integer rounding and exact multidimensional query rules need validation before extrapolating. Extending the same recurrence would also face the explicit routine-adaptation objection. No proof or calculation claimed.

statement_utf8:
For integers $r\ge 3$ and $r-2\ge t\ge 1$, let $\iota_0(t,n;r)$ denote the maximum size of a $t$-intersecting family in an $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraph with all parts of size $n$ and with total intersection of size less than $t$. **The sharp-formula conjecture.** If $n\ge 2$, then

$$
\iota_0(t,n;r)=\max\\{n^{r-t}-(n-1)^{r-t}+t(n-1),(t+2)n^{r-t-1}-(t+1)n^{r-t-2}\\}.
$$

For sufficiently large $n$, the paper proves this formula and identifies a phase transition at $t=\frac{r}{2}-1$; the conjecture asserts that the same extremal formula holds for every $n\ge 2$.
technical_screen: Exact v1 Conjecture 1.13 is withdrawn in v2 introduction after Theorem 1.12. Hou-Hu arXiv2606.06208v1 Theorem 1.1 and Section 3 lower-bound proof explicitly give A_i balls. Executed binary r=6,t=2,n=2 radius-2 ball has 22 edges, min agreement 2 and no fixed coordinate versus max(17,20)=20. It is exactly their A_2, so witness is publicly subsumed, not a discovery.

statement_utf8: Let $k\geq 3$, and let $h_k(n)$ denote the number of induced copies of $C_{2k+1}$ obtained by evenly blowing up $k$ pairwise non-adjacent vertices in a $C_{2k+1}$ on $n$ vertices. For a planar graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, let $\mathscr{H}(G,C_{2k+1})$ be the number of induced copies of $C_{2k+1}$ in $G$. **Optimality conjecture for induced odd cycles.** The maximum of $\mathscr{H}(G,C_{2k+1})$ over all planar graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices is $h_k(n)$. This construction gives the best currently known lower bound for the inducibility of odd cycles in planar graphs; its optimality remains open for all $k\geq 3$.
technical_screen: Exact optimal induced C_(2k+1) count for all k>=3 and all planar orders. Small-order planar exceptions could refute, but would require exact h_k and source size hypotheses first; no alternative planar construction found.

statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be a planar graph with maximum degree $\Delta\ge4$.

**Wang's conjecture.** The D-coloring number of $G$ satisfies

$$
\chi'_D(G)\le
\begin{cases}
9, & \Delta=4,\\
10, & \Delta=5,\\
2\Delta-1, & \Delta\ge6.
\end{cases}
$$

The bound is motivated by planar book constructions and by known upper bounds for the related B-coloring problem; the conjecture remains open only for $6\le\Delta\le32$.
technical_screen: D-edge-coloring definition is not given literally. Unresolved degree interval 6..32 still contains unbounded-order graphs; fixed-degree enumeration is not full scope. No structural planar coloring mechanism identified.

statement_utf8:
Let $S$ be a set of $n$ points in $d$-dimensional space. The **regression depth** of a hyperplane is the minimum number of points intersected by the hyperplane as it undergoes a continuous motion from its initial position to vertical. **Rousseeuw and Hubert's conjecture.** For every $d$-dimensional set of $n$ points, there exists a hyperplane having regression depth

$$
\left\lceil\frac{n}{d+1}\right\rceil.
$$

The conjecture asks for the higher-dimensional analogue of the optimal planar bound, and is motivated by the relation between regression depth and center-point phenomena. The supplied source does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.
technical_screen: All dimensions and point sets, ceil(n/(d+1)) regression depth. This is a classical regression-depth/centerpoint problem; recollection of a public proof is not used as evidence. Need actual primary theorem and conventions for vertical hyperplanes/degenerate sets. No novelty claim.

statement_utf8:
At the Razumov–Stroganov point $q=e^{2i\pi/3}$, take the homogeneous limit $w_i=1$ for all $i$ in the level-one $D_r$ $q$KZ solution, viewed as the Perron–Frobenius eigenvector $\Psi$ of the transfer-matrix Hamiltonian $H_D$. Normalize $\Psi$ so that its smallest entry is $\Psi_{\pi_0}=1$. **Half-turn symmetric alternating-sign-matrix conjecture.** The sum of the entries is the number of half-turn symmetric alternating sign matrices of size $r$:

$$
\sum_\pi\Psi_\pi=A_{HT}(r).
$$

This conjecture connects the homogeneous ground-state vector of the $D_r$ model with half-turn symmetric alternating sign matrices. The source presents the equality as a finding at the Razumov–Stroganov point and provides no proof or resolution.
technical_screen: For every rank r the normalized D_r qKZ ground-state sum is A_HT(r). Exact Hamiltonian, indexing, homogeneous specialization and positivity normalization require primary definitions. Known-looking Razumov-Stroganov identities are not body clearance; no recurrence route established.

statement_utf8:
Let $L$ be a link. Its **unlinking number** $u(L)$ is the minimum number of crossing changes needed to transform $L$ into an unlink, and $u_{BJ}(L)$ denotes its Bernhard–Jablan unlinking number. **Bernhard–Jablan conjecture.** For every link $L$ we have

$$
u(L)=u_{BJ}(L).
$$

The conjecture asserts equality between the classical unlinking number and the Bernhard–Jablan unlinking number; the supplied source does not establish whether it has been resolved.
technical_screen: Equality for every link, not just a knot or table. Public counterexamples are a plausible prior lead but were not fetched or relied on; no source-body clearance. Exhaustive knot computations without exact Bernhard-Jablan conventions would not qualify.

statement_utf8:
Improve the bounds. Is it $o(t^2)$? Perhaps the lower bound is the truth.

\emph{Related results:}

(Phelps--R\"odl) $r_3(P_2, K_t) = \Theta(t^2/\log t)$. This is the
same as giving the minimum independence number of a linear triple system on $n$ points.

(Mubayi--Cooper) $r_3(P_s,K_t) = \Theta(t^2)$ for fixed $s \geq 4$

Here is the construction giving the lower bound for $r_3(P_s,K_4)$ for
$s \geq 4$. Consider the 3-uniform $t^2$-vertex hypergraph with the vertex
set being points of a $t \times t$ grid, i.e., $V = [t] \times [t]$, and
three points form an edge if and only if they form an L-shape, i.e.,

$$
\{(x_1,y_2),(x_1,y_1),(x_2,y_1)\} \quad \text{for all } 1 \le x_1 < x_2 \le t
\text{ and } 1 \le y_1 < y_2 \le t.
$$

This hypergraph has independence number $2t -1$ and is $P_4$-free.
technical_screen: Literal request asks o(t^2) without identifying s in the question sentence, with surrounding P2 and s>=4 results and a likely K4/Kt transcription. AIM route remains parked. Cannot promote an asymptotic target before source scope is restored.

statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree bounded by $\Delta$. For the following choices of Hermitian matrix $M_G$ associated with $G$, what is the maximum multiplicity of the second largest eigenvalue of $M_G$?
For the following choices of Hermitian matrix $M_G$ associated with $G$, what is the maximum multiplicity of the second largest eigenvalue of $M_G$?
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item The adjacency matrix: in this case a sublinear upper bound was proved by, with an improvement in the case of regular graphs provided by and also for the normalized adjacency matrix of general bounded degree graphs. Constructions of graphs establishing lower bounds were given by.
 \item The Laplacian matrix.
 \item Schr\"{o}dinger operators: any matrix of the form $D+A_G$ where $A_G$ is the adjacency matrix and $D$ is an arbitrary diagonal matrix.
 \item Weighted adjacency matrices: any Hermitian matrix $M_G$ such that $M_G[i,j] = 0$ if $\{i,j\}\notin E(G)$. 
\end{enumerate}
technical_screen: Four matrix classes and an unspecified n-dependence for second eigenvalue multiplicity. Connectivity and nonzero-weight requirements matter: disconnected copies or zero matrices trivially inflate multiplicity, but that is a source/domain issue. AIM remains parked; no new result.

statement_utf8: Determine the upper and lower estimates for the growth of entire and meromorphic solutions of algebraic ordinary differential equations (AODE). (This is a classical problem.) For AODEs of first order, it is known that the meromorphic solutions $f$ must have finite order (see Gol'dberg ) and that $(\log r)^2=O(T(r,f))$ (see Eremenko , ). (The latter two references contain a general account of first order AODEs, including modern proofs of some classical results.) The order of entire solutions of first order AODEs is an integral multiple of $\frac{1}{2}$ (see Malmquist ). For AODEs of second order, it is known that the order of entire solutions is positive, see Zimogljad . There is no upper estimate valid for all entire or meromorphic solutions of AODEs of order grreater than one, but there is an old conjecture that $\log |f(z)|\leq exp_n(|z|)$ for entire solutions $f$ of an AODE of order $n$. (A. Eremenko)
technical_screen: Broad AODE growth problem plus an iterated exponential conjecture for all orders. Polynomial/constant exceptional solutions also need exact quantifiers. No differential-algebra mechanism or full uniform growth bound found.

statement_utf8: Erd\"os and Newman conjectured that if $$ f(z)=\sum^n_{k=0}a_kz^k,\hspace{1cm} |a_k|=1, \hspace{1cm}0\leq k\leq n, $$ then there is an absolute constant $c$ such that $$ \max_{|z|=1}|f(z)|>(1+c)n^{1/2}. $$ The weaker form of our conjecture stated that ([source label: D2]) holds if we assume \linebreak \mbox{$a_k=\pm1$} (Problem 4.13). A stronger form would be that ([source label: D2]) holds even if \mbox{$f(z)=\sum^n_{k=1}a_{n_k}z^{n_k}$}, $n_k$ natural numbers, $|a_{n_k}|=1$. However, ([source label: D2]) was disproved by Kahane (no citation). In fact, he showed that, given that $\varepsilon>0$, there are polynomials of the form ([source label: D1]) for which $$ \max_{|z|=1}|f(z)|<n^{1/2}+O(n^{(3/10)+\varepsilon})\hspace{1cm}\text{ as }n\to\infty. $$ Show that $n^{(3/10)+\varepsilon}$ cannot be replaced by $n^\varepsilon$ in ([source label: D3]). Is there any $n$-th degree polynomial of the form ([source label: D1]) for which $$ \min_{|z|=1}|f(z)|>(1-\varepsilon)n^{1/2} $$ for every positive $\varepsilon$ if $n>n_0(\varepsilon)$? Perhaps there is an $n$-th degree polynomial of the form ([source label: D1]), for which, for all $z$, $|z|=1$, $$ (1-\varepsilon)n^{1/2}<|f(z)|<(1+\varepsilon)n^{1/2}. $$ In fact, ([source label: D5]) could possibly hold with $n^{1/2}+O(1)$ on the left and right. It would be worthwhile to determine if ([source label: D2]) holds for $a_k=\pm1$ and for $a_{n_k}=\pm1$. (P. Erd\"os and D. Newman)
technical_screen: Includes already-disproved unimodular lower conjecture, sharper errors, ultraflat existence, and a separate real-sign problem. The literal text itself attributes a Kahane refutation; that does not settle the remaining clauses. No full-record outcome or primary-body clearance.

statement_utf8:
(The corona conjecture) Let $D$ be an arbitrary domain in the plane that supports non-constant bounded analytic functions. Suppose that $f_1(z),\ldots, f_n(z)$ are bounded and analytic in $D$ and satisfy \[\sum^n_{
u=1}|f_
u(z)|\geq\delta>0\] in $D$. Can one find bounded analytic functions $g_
u(z)$ in $D$ such that \[\sum^n_{
u=1}f_
u(z)g_
u(z)\equiv1\] in $D$? When $D$ is a disc, Carleson proved that the answer is `yes', and the result extends to finitely connected domains. The result is also known to be true for certain infinitely connected domains (see Behrens , Gamelin ), but false for general Riemann surfaces of infinite genus (Cole, unpublished). Presumably the answer for the general plane domain is negative. Proofs of all positive results depend on Carleson's theorem. (L. Zalcman)
technical_screen: Corona Bezout solution for every finitely generated bounded analytic datum on every planar domain supporting nonconstant functions. Disc/finitely connected cases are explicitly known; general Riemann-surface failures do not supply a planar-domain counterexample.

statement_utf8: Goluzin has shown that, if $g(z)\prec f(z)$ in $\mathbb{D}$, then \[M_2(r,g')\leq M_2(r,f'),\hspace{1cm}0\leq r\leq\frac{1}{2}.\] Here, for $p > 0$, \[M_p(r,h)=\Big(\frac{1}{2\pi}\int^{2\pi}_0|h(re^{i\theta})|^p\,d\theta\Big)^{1/p}.\] The result is not necessarily true if $r > \frac{1}{2}$, as $f(z) = z, g(z) = z^2$ shows, though it follows from a theorem of Littlewood that, for all $p$, \[M_p(r,g)\leq M_p(r,f),\hspace{1cm} 0 < r < 1.\] Find the largest number $r_p, 0 < r_p < 1$, independent of $f$ and $g$ so that \[M_p(r,g')\leq M_p(r,f'),\hspace{1cm} 0<r<r_p,\] if $g\prec f$. Note: If $g(z) \prec f(z)$ in $\mathbb{D}$, then $g(z) = f(\phi(z))$ so that \[|g'(z)|\leq |f'(\phi(z))|,\hspace{1cm}|z|\leq\sqrt{2}-1,\] (see Carath\'eodory ). Thus if $h(z) = f'(\phi(z))$ then $h\prec f'$ so that, by Littlewood's theorem, $M_p(r,g') \leq M_p(r,h) \leq M_p(r,f')$ for $p > 0, r \leq\sqrt{2}-1$. This improves what one gets if one applied ([source label: C5.2]) to the $p$-th means since $\sqrt{2}-1>3-\sqrt{8}$; but it may not be best possible. (P. L. Duren)
technical_screen: Find sharp radius r_p for every p>0 and all subordinate pairs. z,z^2 gives only upper bound 1/2; Schwarz/Littlewood yields sqrt(2)-1 lower bound already in statement. Neither closes p-dependent gap, so no parameter/helper credit.

statement_utf8: Hentgartner and Schobe and Goodman and Saff have shown that if $f(z) = z + a_2z^2 +\ldots$ maps $\mathbb{D}$ univalently onto a domain $G_1$ that is convex in the direction of the imaginary axis (CIA), then $G_r = \{f(|z| < r)\}$ is not necessarily CIA for all $r$, $r < 1$, or even for $r$ bigger than some constant. [(a)] ; Find $\sup\{r : G_r \text{ is necessarily CIA}\}$. (A result of Goodman and Saff suggests that this is $\sqrt{2}-1$.) ; Find reasonable sufficient conditions on $G_1$ (or, equivalently, on $f$) that imply that $G_r$ is in CIA for all $r$ in $(0,1)$. ; Suppose that we slit $G_1$ along the real axis and let $G'$, $G''$ be those two components of the resulting family of domains that have $0$ on their boundaries. If $G_1 = G' \cup G''$, does it necessarily follow that $G_r$ is CIA for all $r$ in $(0,1)$? ; If $G_1$ is CIA but $G_{r_0}$ is not CIA, is it true that $G_r$ is not CIA for $r_0 < r < 1$? (D. A. Brannan)
technical_screen: Four independent CIA-domain questions about sharp radius, sufficient conditions, slit geometry and persistence after failure. The suggested sqrt(2)-1 is not a proof, and establishing only a familiar sufficient class would not resolve full record.

statement_utf8: This problem is equivalent to Problem 7.9 due to Gehring and Reich about best bounds for area distribution under quasiconformal mapping. Let $E$ denote a measurable subset of the unit disc $\mathbb{D}$, $m$ denote $2$-dimensional measure, and define \[f_E(z)=-\frac{1}{\pi}\int\int_E\frac{dm(w)}{(w-z)^2},\hspace{1cm}z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus E.\] Thus, $f_E$ is the $2$-dimensional Hilbert transform of the characteristic function of $E$. It follows from the Calder\'on-Zygmund theory of singular integrals that there are constants $a$ and $b$ such that \[\int\int_{\mathbb{D}\setminus E}|f_E|\,dm\leq am(E)\log\frac{\pi}{m(E)}+bm(E)\] for every $E$. The problem is to find the smallest possible $a$ (for which there exists some $b$ such that the inequality holds for every $E\subset\mathbb{D}$). Consideration of $E=\{z:|z|<\delta\}$ for small $\delta$ shows that $a=1$ would be best possible, and this is conjectured by Gehring and Reich. An analogous sharp inequality for sets $E\subset[-1,1]$ and $1$-dimensional Hilbert transforms \[f_E(x)=-\frac{1}{\pi}\int_E\frac{dt}{x-t}\] is known, and can be proved either by a subordination argument or by use of a theorem of Stein and Weiss. (A. Baernstein)
technical_screen: Optimal logarithmic coefficient for all measurable subsets of disc. Disc E already gives necessary a>=1; it does not prove sharp upper bound. Quasiconformal area-distortion theorems are prior leads requiring actual derivative/asymptotic bridge; none inspected.

statement_utf8: (T. Kohno) Construct explicitly a universal invariant of finite type for links in Σ × [0, 1] with values in AΣ. In the case of genus 0 the above problem is solved by Kontsevic h integral. In higher genus case a suggestion for a construction of a univer sal invariant was given by Deligne at Oberwolfach meeting 1995. In the case of a punctured surface the problem was solved by Andersen, Mattes and Reshe tikhin. Let G be a simple Lie group and MG(Σ) the moduli space of G flat connections on Σ. The space of smooth functions on MG(Σ) denoted by C(MG(Σ)) has a structure of a Poisson algebra coming from a symplectic stru cture on MG(Σ). The algebraAΣ has also a Poisson algebra structure (see [8]). If each compo nent ofAΣ is colored by a representation of G, then there is a natural Poisson algebra homomorphism τ:AΣ → C(MG(Σ)). Problem 3.23 is related to the following problem.
technical_screen: Universal finite-type invariant in A_Sigma for links in closed higher-genus product surfaces. Punctured-surface and genus-zero cases are explicitly source-known; gluing across punctures requires a full algebraic invariance bridge, not supplied.

statement_utf8:
Find a way to effectively compute the Kauffman–Radford–Hennings
(KRH) invariants for three-manifolds via right
integrals on finite dimensional Hopf algebras . Find a way
to categorify the Kauffman–Radford–Hennings invariants for all
finite dimensional quasitriangular Hopf algebras. The KRH invariants
are actually invariants of rotational virtual links that are also,
after normalization, invariant under the moves of the Kirby
calculus. In this way, they give invariants of three manifolds and
virtual three manifolds. The formulation of the KRH invariants in
terms of integrals for finite dimensional Hopf algebras is very
elegant, but computation is very difficult. Thus these invariants
form a challenge for both virtual and classical knot theory. It is
worth pointing out again, that the proper domain for all
quantum link invariants is rotational virtual knot theory. Thus,
this problem about the KRH invariants is a test case for the
structure of quantum link invariants as a whole.
technical_screen: Both effective KRH computation and categorification for all finite-dimensional quasitriangular Hopf algebras are requested. Straight tensor contraction only restates an existing invariant algorithm; categorification and normalization remain substantial independent obligations.

statement_utf8:
Is there any algorithm for recognition whether two graph-links are
equivalent or not? Our conjecture is “no”. The idea behind that is
that graph-links are complicated enough, and possibly, they contain
sufficiently many degrees of freedom to include something like
Turing machines. All mathematics is roughly split into the
recognizable one (low-dimensional topology, hyperbolic groups,
decidability) and the non-recognizable one (topology of dimension
$4$ and higher, arbitrary finitely presentable groups, Turing
machines etc). The usual argument for undecidability for finitely
presented group allows one to construct some universal (semi)groups
which includes the apparatus of the Turing machines. We think that
graph-links are enough complicated to include similar things: they
contain arbitrary graphs, and Reidemeister moves, in principle,
could play the role of “rules for formal languages” or “group
relations”. It seems unlikely that Reidemeister moves collapse
graph-links to anything simple enough because of the parity
considerations: there are “irreducibly odd” graph-links which are
stable in the sense that every equivalent graph contains the initial
graph as a subgraph.
technical_screen: Algorithmic decidability or an undecidability reduction for arbitrary graph-links under Reidemeister moves. Enumerating moves gives only semidecidability. Universal-machine speculation is not a reduction and no invariant-normal-form decision procedure was found.

Critical points of L are most likely not isolated; however, explain the change in the homotopy type of L −1 [0,t ] as t passes through a critical value. For example, take the case g = 2. Spaces added at infinity are Y 1 1×Y 1 1×S1 = H2× H2×S1 and the restriction of L to such a set factors through H2× H2 where it has a unique minimum and no other critical points. Thus this set contains a “mincircle”. Hope. A point of Y 2 is a local minimum of L iﬀ it belongs to one of these mincircles. In addition there are isolated critical points of index 1 that connect up these circles in a tree-like pattern. Thus Y 2 and Y2 are homotopy equivalent to a wedge of circles, one circle for every splitting, recovering the theorem of Mess mentioned above. 2the smallest dimension of a space homotopy equivalent to Yg 1. statement_utf8: (Presentation for level L structures). Give an explicit finite presentation for Modg[L]. Once one has such a presentation, it seems likely that it would fit well into the framework of Pitsch’s proof [ Pi] that rank( H2(Modg,1, Z))≤ 1 for g≥ 4. Note that Pitsch’s proof was extended to punctured and bordered case by Korkmaz-Stipsicsz; see [ Ko]. What Pitsch does is to begin with an explicit, finite presentation of Mod g,1, and then to apply Hopf’s formula for groups Γ presented as the quotient of a free group F by the normal closure R of the relators: H2(Γ, Z) = R∩ [F,F ] [F,R ] (17) In other words, elements of H2(Γ, Z) come precisely from commutators which are relators, except for the trivial ones. Amazingly, one needs only write the form of an arbitrary element of the numerator in (17), and a few tricks reduces the computation of (an upper bound for) space of solutions to computing the rank of an integer matrix. In our case this approach seems feasible, especially with computer computation, at least for small L. Of course one hopes to find a general pattern.
technical_screen: For arbitrary genus and level, explicit Mod_g[L] presentation is requested. Reidemeister-Schreier from a known presentation and finite symplectic quotient is a generic finite-index algorithm; without a specified structural efficiency goal it is a routine adaptation, not a new full-scope discovery.

statement_utf8: Forg,h≥ 2, does there exist a short exact sequence: 1→π1(Σg)→ Γ→π1(Σh)→ 1 for which Γ is a word hyperbolic group? Arguing as in the proof of Theorem 4.2, it follows that such an extension defines a purely pseudo-Anosov surface subgroup of Γ g. However, even in this case, little is known. We make two comments in this regard. 1. One result is that Γ cannot be the fundamental group of a closed complex hyperbolic surface. As described in [ 20], this follows from [ 25], on showing that if Γ is as decribed, then there is a non-singular holomorphic fibration X = H2 C/Γ→ Σh that induces the short exact sequence (see also [ 17]). 2. The following idea to construct purely pseudo-Anosov surface subgroups was described to me by Ian Agol. In [ 40], Thurston proves the following result (see [ 40] for terminology and further details). 17. Surface subgroups of mapping class groups 283
technical_screen: For g,h>=2 seek surface-by-surface word-hyperbolic extension; quantifier whether all pairs or some pairs requires primary context. Purely pseudo-Anosov surface subgroups are already an explicit obstruction in statement. No construction or uniform nonexistence argument found.

statement_utf8: Find explicit way of calculating d1(ϕ) for any given element ϕ ∈ Kg. In particular, determine whether the Magnus representation Ig,1→GL(2g; Z[H]) of the Torelli group detectsd1 or not. Suzuki [ 103] proved that the Magnus representation of the Torelli group mentioned above is not faithful so that it may happen that the intersection of the kernel of the Magnus representation withKg is not contained in the kernel of d1. We may also ask whether the representation of the hyperelliptic mapping class group given by Jones [ 45], restricted to the intersection of this group withKg, detects d1 or not (cf. Kasahara [ 46] for a related work for the case g = 2). There are also various interesting works related to the class d1 such as Endo [ 14] and Morifuji [ 71] treating the hyperelliptic mapping class group, Kitano [ 54] as well as Hain and Reed [ 33]. Recently Biss and Farb [ 5] proved that the group Kg is not finitely generated for all g≥ 3 (K2 is known to be an infinitely generated free group by Mess [ 69]). However it is still not yet known whether the abelianization H1(Kg) is finitely generated or not (cf. Problem 2.2 of [ 80]). Finally we would like to mention that Kawazumi [ 50] is developing a theory of harmonic Mag- nus expansions which gives in particular a system of diﬀerential forms representing the Mumford- Morita-Miller classes on the universal family of curves over the moduli space Mg.
technical_screen: Compute d1 for every Johnson-kernel element and decide detection by Magnus/Jones restrictions. Representation nonfaithfulness does not imply non-detection of d1. Historical Biss-Farb assertion also needs current verification; no explicit kernel element with nonzero d1 or general algorithm supplied.
